claim: In the six months ending March 2026, only 68% of Android switchers who bought a new iPhone chose a current flagship model (iPhone 17/17 Air/17 Pro/17 Pro Max), versus 80% of legacy iPhone owners upgrading.
stance_target: ASP and upgrade-cycle implications of a growing switcher cohort
quoted_support: In the six-month period ending in March 2026, 68% of Android switchers bought one of the new flagship iPhone 17 models: 17, 17 Air, 17 Pro, or 17 Pro Max (Chart 1). In comparison, 80% of legacy iPhone owners who bought a new iPhone chose one of those models.

claim: Around 12% of iPhone buyers in the same six-month window came from Android, consistent with the 11-15% band reported elsewhere by CIRP.
stance_target: Stability of the Android-to-iPhone switcher pool
quoted_support: Last week Consumer Intelligence Research Partners (CIRP) updated its switching (and loyalty) analysis to show around 12% of iPhone buyers came from the Android operating system.

claim: First-time/switcher iPhone buyers under-index on flagship models because baseline iOS functionality (iMessage, FaceTime) satisfies their needs, without requiring the newest hardware.
stance_target: Mechanism behind lower ASP mix among switchers
quoted_support: They don't feel the need or perhaps fully understand the appeal of the newest, leading-edge iPhone models. Just getting iMessage and FaceTime is enough.
